intro: Terms that look alike are where multiple choice catches people. Compare them side by side, then drill: you get a statement and pick the term it describes.

terms.name: Rules and procedures
terms.means: COBIT and COSO: they answer 'How do I keep control over my finance?'
clues: COBIT and COSO belong here.
They answer: how do I keep control over my finance?
COSO has the widest scope in the coverage picture.

terms.name: Best practices
terms.means: ITIL, BiSL, ASL, ISM and MOF: they answer 'How do I organize my IT processes?'
clues: ITIL, BiSL, ASL, ISM and MOF belong here.
They answer: how do I organize my IT processes?
ITIL is drawn on the 'how' side of the coverage picture.

terms.name: Standards
terms.means: ISO, ANSI and BSI: they answer 'How do I control my quality?'
clues: ISO, ANSI and BSI belong here.
They answer: how do I control my quality?
ISO 9000 and ISO 27001 are of this kind.

terms.name: COBIT
terms.means: Control Objectives for Information Technology: 2 areas, 5 domains, 37 processes, 210 practices, 1112 activities.
clues: It has 5 domains and 37 processes.
210 governance and management practices and 1112 activities.
The framework listed with ISO and CMMI for all subjects, with rules and procedures about finance.

terms.name: CMMI
terms.means: Capability Maturity Model Integration, from Carnegie Mellon University: 5 maturity levels, 24 process areas.
clues: It has 5 maturity levels and 24 process areas.
Developed by Carnegie Mellon University.
Designed for rating and comparing organisations, or for process improvement.

terms.name: ITIL
terms.means: 3 process clusters and 34 processes. Listed for IT infrastructure maintenance.
clues: It has 3 process clusters and 34 processes.
The framework listed for IT infrastructure maintenance.
ISO 20000 has 30 processes 'like' it.

terms.name: ISO 27001
terms.means: Information security management: 114 controls (policies).
clues: It lists 114 controls.
The standard for information security management.
The framework listed for IT security.

terms.name: ISO 20000
terms.means: IT service management (BS 15000): 30 processes, like ITIL.
clues: It has 30 processes, like ITIL.
Also known as BS 15000.
The ISO standard for IT service management.

terms.name: ITIL
terms.means: IT infrastructure maintenance.
clues: The framework listed for IT infrastructure maintenance.

terms.name: Scrum
terms.means: New software.
clues: The framework listed for new software.

terms.name: DevOps
terms.means: Running software.
clues: The framework listed for running software.

terms.name: PRINCE2
terms.means: IT projects.
clues: The framework listed for IT projects.

terms.name: TOGAF
terms.means: IT architecture.
clues: The framework listed for IT architecture.

terms.name: LEAN
terms.means: Process improvement.
clues: The framework listed for process improvement.

terms.name: ISO 27001
terms.means: IT security.
clues: The framework listed for IT security.

terms.name: SPO
terms.means: Service providing organisation: the IT provider.
clues: The IT provider.
Its utilization rate is billable hours as a percentage of working hours.
Uses consultative selling and can lose its innovative spirit when it focuses on growth.

terms.name: SRO
terms.means: Service receiving organisation: the customer, the users.
clues: The customer and the users.
It has to assess the candidate providers thoroughly.
It must match its structure to the provider's through organisational alignment.

terms.name: Verticals
terms.means: Industry-specific (content-specific) services at application or functional level.
clues: Services that are specific to a branch or industry.
Services at application or functional level.
Business managers sit on this side.

terms.name: Horizontals
terms.means: General technical services (infrastructure, testing, BI) that serve all customers across the verticals.
clues: Infrastructure, testing and BI.
General technical services that serve all customers.
Process managers sit on this side.

terms.name: Supporting services
terms.means: The general supporting departments.
clues: The traditional supporting departments.
General supporting departments of the provider.
The third column of how an SPO is structured.

terms.name: Fixed price contract
terms.means: An agreed set of activities for a fixed price.
clues: An agreed set of activities for a fixed price.

terms.name: Time and materials contract
terms.means: Pay staff per hour and for materials.
clues: Staff is paid per hour, and materials are paid for.

terms.name: Staff augmentation
terms.means: Hire professional staff.
clues: Hiring professional staff.

terms.name: Low-end disruption
terms.means: Simple, cheap products win at the low end because established companies add features too fast. No new technology.
clues: Aldi, Ryanair and IKEA.
Established companies add features at too high a pace, so simple cheap products win.
It needs no new technology.

terms.name: New-market disruption
terms.means: Extending an innovation to a new market, often with internet or mobile technology.
clues: eBay, Uber and the e-bike.
An innovation extended to a new market.
New technology, many times internet or mobile technology in existing markets.

terms.name: Top-down disruption
terms.means: New products that outperform the existing ones, sold at a higher price at first.
clues: Apple, Tesla, PlayStation and Samsung.
Products that outperform the existing ones.
Sold at a higher price in the beginning.

terms.name: Sustaining innovation
terms.means: An existing company defends itself by modernizing its old services or products.
clues: Chain stores starting webshops.
How existing companies defend against disruptive newcomers.
Modernizing old services or products.

terms.name: Product innovation
terms.means: Innovation in the primary product, e.g. Apple, Tesla.
clues: The primary aspect: Apple and Tesla are examples.
Innovation in what is sold.

terms.name: Process innovation
terms.means: Innovation in the supporting process, e.g. the Toyota production process, Dell, Alibaba.
clues: The supporting aspect: the Toyota production process (LEAN) is an example.
Dell and Alibaba are examples.
Innovation in how the work is done.

terms.name: New combinations of existing elements
terms.means: E.g. coffee pads, e-bikes, agricultural drones, smart watches, hybrid cars.
clues: Coffee pads and e-bikes are examples.
Agricultural drones, smart watches and hybrid cars.
Existing elements put together in a new way.

terms.name: Release Train Engineer (RTE)
terms.means: Coordinator of the ART, facilitates the ART meetings, like a team's Scrum Master.
clues: Coordinates the ART and facilitates the ART meetings.
Leads the PI Planning retrospective.
Comparable with a team's Scrum Master.

terms.name: Product Owner (program level)
terms.means: The PO of the program.
clues: The PO of the program.
Attends the weekly PO Sync.
Works at program level, above the teams' POs.

terms.name: System Architect
terms.means: Ensures technical integrity and defines the architectural guidelines for the teams.
clues: Ensures technical integrity.
Defines the architectural guidelines for the teams.
Presents the architecture vision and roadmap on PI Planning day 1.

terms.name: Scrum of Scrums Master
terms.means: The facilitator of the team Scrum Master meetings.
clues: The facilitator of the team Scrum Master meetings.
Works with the Scrum Masters of the teams.
Facilitates the Scrum of Scrums.

groups.title: Scrum at Scale: roles and events

terms.name: Scrum of Scrums Master (SoSM)
terms.means: Facilitates the teams.
clues: Facilitates the teams.
Takes part in the Scaled Daily Scrum and the weekly Scrum of Scrums.

terms.name: Chief Product Owner (CPO)
terms.means: Coordinates the PO team.
clues: Coordinates the PO team.
Prioritizes the one backlog together with the POs.

terms.name: Executive Action Team (EAT)
terms.means: CPO, SoSM, CEO and company managers: resolves escalated impediments and takes strategic decisions.
clues: Consists of the CPO, SoSM, CEO and company managers.
Resolves escalated impediments and takes strategic decisions.
Facilitates team clusters in the double-scaled setting.

terms.name: Executive MetaScrum (EMS)
terms.means: The CPO and the POs prioritize the one backlog, at least once per sprint.
clues: A meeting of the CPO and the POs.
Prioritizes the backlog that is shared by all teams.
Meets at least once per sprint.

terms.name: Scaled Daily Scrum
terms.means: At least one representative per team.
clues: Daily, 15 minutes, one representative per team plus the SoSM.
Focus on cross-team progress and impediments.

terms.name: Scaled Retrospective
terms.means: All Scrum Masters of each team.
clues: All the Scrum Masters of the teams take part.
Improves processes across groups.

terms.name: SAFe
terms.means: The elaborate framework: ART, PI, RTE, System Architect.
clues: The elaborate one of the two.
Uses an Agile Release Train of 5 to 12 teams and a Program Increment.
Has a two-day PI Planning event and an Inspect & Adapt workshop.

terms.name: Scrum at Scale
terms.means: The minimalistic framework: SoSM, CPO, EAT, one backlog.
clues: The minimalistic one of the two.
One backlog for all the teams.
Has an Executive MetaScrum and an Executive Action Team.

groups.title: Audit: the auditor or the organization?

terms.name: The auditor
terms.means: Plans, analyzes and reports the findings, issues the final report.
clues: Plans the audit.
Analyzes and reports the findings.
Issues the final report.
Reports the identified shortcomings.

terms.name: The organization
terms.means: Responds to the findings and makes the improvement plan.
clues: Responds to the findings.
Makes the improvement plan.
Executes the planned measures.

terms.name: Share of services in-house
terms.means: Perform at least 20% of the IT services in-house.
clues: Perform at least 20% of the IT services in-house.
A share of the services, not of the people.
Let IT staff spread across all IT functions of the SPO to learn the outsourced work.

terms.name: Share of own personnel
terms.means: Agree on a minimum percentage (for example 25%) of SRO personnel, and keep SRO personnel on key positions.
clues: A minimum percentage of SRO personnel, for example 25%.
Keep SRO personnel on key positions.
Business continuity knowledge retention testing belongs here.

terms.name: Day 1
terms.means: Business context and visions, team breakouts #1, draft plan review, management review.
clues: Business context by Business Owners and Product Management.
Teams identify stories, estimate story points and identify risks.
Teams present draft plans.
The evening management review for leadership only.

terms.name: Day 2
terms.means: Team breakouts #2, final plan review and confidence vote, PI objectives, program board, retrospective.
clues: Teams finalize plans and align dependencies.
Final plan review with a confidence vote.
The program board is finalized.
The PI Planning retrospective, led by the RTE.

groups.title: BCG matrix: star, cow, question mark or dog?

terms.name: Star
terms.means: High market growth and high market share: invest.
clues: High market growth and a high market share.
The advice in the BCG matrix is to invest.

terms.name: Cow
terms.means: Low market growth and high market share.
clues: Low market growth but a high market share.
It is drawn with a dollar sign.

terms.name: Question mark
terms.means: High market growth and low market share: prioritize or divest.
clues: High market growth but a low market share.
The arrows say prioritize or divest.
A very promising prototype that has no market share yet.

terms.name: Dog
terms.means: Low market growth and low market share: kill.
clues: Low market growth and a low market share.
The advice in the BCG matrix is to kill it.

terms.name: Heavy pyramid
terms.means: More experienced people: for tough jobs.
clues: Relatively many experienced people.
The right set-up for tough jobs.

terms.name: Lean pyramid
terms.means: Few experienced people and many freshers: for light jobs.
clues: Few experienced people and many freshers.
The right set-up for light jobs.

groups.title: Weekly or daily: the scaled meetings

terms.name: SAFe Scrum of Scrums
terms.means: Weekly, at ART level: Scrum Masters, the RTE and others with dependencies.
clues: It takes place weekly at ART level.
Scrum Masters, the RTE and others with dependencies attend.

terms.name: S@S Scaled Daily Scrum
terms.means: Daily, 15 minutes: one representative per team plus the SoSM.
clues: It is held daily for 15 minutes.
One representative per team plus the Scrum of Scrums Master.
